props.title: The Street Fighter
props.initialSlug: Brutal martial artist fights crime in deadly underworld

sections.content: The Street Fighter (1974) marks a pivotal moment in martial arts cinema, earning an X-rating for its unprecedented violence and launching Sonny Chiba as an international action star. Unlike the honorable warriors in Enter the Dragon (1973) or the stoic heroes of Five Fingers of Death (1972), Chiba's Terry Tsurugi is a ruthless antihero who'll crush throats and rip out organs. The film's brutal fight choreography and unflinching gore influenced later directors like Quentin Tarantino, who referenced it directly in True Romance (1993) and cast Chiba in Kill Bill: Vol. 1 (2003).

sections.content: The film's success spawned an entire subgenre of grittier, more violent martial arts films throughout the 1970s. The Street Fighter series contrasted sharply with the more traditional kung fu films coming out of Hong Kong, like The Chinese Connection (1972) and The Big Boss (1971). Where Bruce Lee's characters fought for justice and honor, Chiba's Tsurugi was a mercenary whose brutal techniques and questionable morality prefigured the darker action antiheroes of the 1980s.

Director Shigehiro Ozawa's unflinching camera work during fight scenes set new standards for martial arts cinematography. Unlike the quick-cut editing prevalent in later action films, Ozawa held shots longer to showcase Chiba's actual martial arts prowess. This approach influenced directors like John Carpenter, who paid homage to this style in Big Trouble in Little China (1986) and Isaac Florentine's later works like Undisputed II: Last Man Standing (2006). sections.content: The film's impact extends far beyond martial arts cinema. Its graphic violence and morally ambiguous protagonist helped pave the way for harder-edged action films like First Blood (1982) and Above the Law (1988). Chiba's portrayal of Tsurugi established a new archetype of the antihero martial artist, influencing characters in films like Bloodsport (1988) and The Man from Nowhere (2010).
